results.q: What happens when a request times out?
answer: When a request times out, `ModbusTransport.UnicastMessage<T>()` detects the error and calls `LoggingExtensions.Error()`, logs the exception type, then calls `ModbusTransport.Sleep()` which waits using `Task.Wait`. If the retry count is exceeded (`attempt++ > _retries`), the method stops early and does not call `Sleep()` or `WaitToRetryMilliseconds.get()`.

Losing the data is detected in ModbusTransport.UnicastMessage<T>() (NModbus/IO/ModbusTransport.cs:202), which checks `e is FormatException || e is NotImplementedException || e is TimeoutException || e is IOException || e is SocketException`.

When that happens it calls LoggingExtensions.Error() (which calls IModbusLogger.Log(LoggingLevel.Error, message) (line 33)); calls Exception.GetType; calls ModbusTransport.Sleep() (which calls Task.Wait (line 331)); calls WaitToRetryMilliseconds.get().

ModbusTransport.UnicastMessage<T>() also stops early when `attempt++ > _retries` (line 210), which skips ModbusTransport.Sleep(), WaitToRetryMilliseconds.get() — so without fresh valid data it does not reach those calls either.
